issues.title: Is sync from the old version possible?
issues.still_relevant_reason: Upstream has no sync. Directory upload always creates a new folder (src/main.rs:196, src/files/upload.rs:136-199). Recursive download only skips MD5-identical files and never deletes extras (src/files/download.rs:166-168). fork:toutizes implements `download --sync` and `upload --overwrite/--sync`, with an MD5 skip and deletion of extra files (forks/toutizes/src/main.rs:208-223, 273-292; src/files/upload.rs:147-178, 219-220; src/files/download.rs:180-184).
issues.recommendation: Adopt toutizes's overwrite and sync semantics, ported onto the dodomorandi dependency stack. Keep --dry-run, require an explicit flag or confirmation before deleting, and define the behavior for duplicate names on Drive (toutizes currently errors out).
issues.notes: The last comment is from toutizes, the fork's author. Skipping MD5-identical files avoids re-transferring unchanged data, a large speed win for repeat backups. Caution: toutizes made the upload file_path mandatory, which drops stdin upload (#23).

issues.title: Needs verification

They say nothing about the 'Needs verification' status or the 'Google hasn't verified this app' screen. The steps also describe the pre-2025 Cloud Console consent-screen UI, which is now the Google Auth Platform (Branding/Audience/Data access/Clients).
issues.recommendation: Rewrite the credentials guide for the current Google Auth Platform UI. Add an FAQ covering: 'Needs verification' is harmless for personal use (under 100 users); how to get past the unverified-app warning; why Testing mode expires refresh tokens after 7 days.

issues.title: Upload directory creates a new one instead of overriding
issues.still_relevant_reason: A new folder per upload is documented behavior (src/main.rs:196), but `files update <id> <dir>` still panics. update opens the path with no is_dir check (src/files/update.rs:44, src/common/file_helper.rs:14-19), and the resumable loop calls read_to_end().unwrap() (google-apis-common lib.rs:687; the same line exists in google-apis-common 8.0.0, so dodomorandi panics too). The proper error the maintainer promised never landed.
addressed_by: fork:toutizes (partial: upload --overwrite/--sync reuses the existing Drive folder)
issues.recommendation: Add an is_dir guard to update, and before any upload, that returns a clear error (small). Provide merge-into-existing-folder through the sync work in #16 (toutizes semantics).
issues.notes: Related: #69 (recursive update) and #16 (sync).

issues.title: Error on download recursive if some file contain slash (/) character
issues.still_relevant_reason: Drive names are joined into local paths unsanitized (src/common/file_tree_drive.rs:154-162, 225-227; src/files/download.rs:123, 163-164). A '/' in a name creates missing subdirectories (os error 2). A name like '../x' or an absolute '/etc/x' escapes the destination, because PathBuf::join replaces the whole path when given an absolute component (verified locally). A shared folder can therefore make gdrive write arbitrary files. Neither fork sanitizes names (dodomorandi src/common/file_tree_drive.rs:125-133; toutizes src/common/disk_item.rs:72-75, and drive_names.rs:34 carries the comment 'MAYBE: handle / in drive filenames?').
issues.recommendation: Add a sanitize_component() applied to every Drive name before joining. It should replace '/' and '\\' with '_' (on Windows also <>:"|?*, trailing dots/spaces and reserved names), reject '.', '..' and empty names, and truncate to 255 bytes (#53). Then assert that the final path stays under the canonical destination root. Warn on every rename and de-duplicate colliding names.
issues.notes: Security issue: path traversal and arbitrary file write during recursive download. download_directory writes files without the --overwrite check (only the root folder is checked), so traversal can clobber existing files. The same fix covers #53 (Filename too long).

issues.title: Triggers recursive Virus-Scan
issues.still_relevant_reason: gdrive has no antivirus interaction. The scan was most likely local AV/Defender reacting to an unsigned binary (README.md:33 says the binaries are not code-signed).
issues.recommendation: Close. Code-signing the Windows and macOS release binaries (a release-CI task) would reduce AV and SmartScreen reports like this.

issues.title: Problems when adding google account to gdrive
issues.still_relevant_reason: The token exchange after the localhost:8085 redirect times out when Google can't be reached directly (the reporter is behind the GFW). gdrive builds its own hyper clients, with no proxy support, for both the API hub and the yup-oauth2 authenticator (src/hub.rs:33-40, 64-71), so HTTP(S)_PROXY and system proxies are ignored.
issues.recommendation: Fix through proxy support (#26): build one shared client that honors HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY/NO_PROXY and the Windows/macOS system proxy, and pass it to both DriveHub and InstalledFlowAuthenticator::with_client. Add a connect timeout so the command fails fast and suggests a proxy.
issues.notes: PR #141 claims to fix #21/#26/#59/#74, but it uses hyper-proxy 0.9 on hyper 0.14. On the modern stack, use the hyper-util 0.1.21 client-proxy feature (Matcher::from_env/from_system plus the Tunnel/SocksV5 connectors) or reqwest.

issues.title: Every Week Gdrive requires permisssion
issues.still_relevant_reason: The root cause is Google's 7-day refresh-token expiry for consent screens in Testing mode, and the docs now say to publish (docs/create_google_api_credentials.md:30-32). The CLI still gives no hint. When the refresh fails, yup-oauth2 silently falls back to the interactive flow (yup-oauth2 authenticator.rs:143-151 in 8.1.0, the same in 12.1.2) and gdrive prints the consent URL (src/hub.rs:105-111), which hangs unattended scripts and cron jobs.
issues.recommendation: Keep the doc step. Detect invalid_grant or a failed refresh and exit non-zero with a hint ('consent screen in Testing mode? re-run gdrive account add'). Never start the interactive flow outside `account add` or when stdin is not a TTY (ties into #147, non-interactive mode).
issues.notes: The last comment asks about Google verification. Related: #17, #35, #129.

issues.title: Support for uploading file from stdin?
issues.still_relevant_reason: PR #41 (merged 2023-07-16) reads stdin when the path is omitted (src/main.rs:185-186; src/files/upload.rs:61-69; src/common/file_helper.rs:6-12). Gaps remain. The issue's own `gdrive files upload -` still fails because '-' is opened as a file, and --help doesn't mention stdin. With no --name option, the Drive file is named after the mktemp UUID temp file (src/common/file_info.rs:22-26) and gets an octet-stream MIME type. stdin is fully buffered to disk before the upload starts.
issues.recommendation: Treat the original request as done and follow up: add `--name` (required or defaulted for stdin), accept '-' as an alias, and document stdin in --help. Optionally stream stdin through a resumable upload with unknown total length instead of the temp file. Don't adopt toutizes's mandatory file_path, which removes stdin support.
issues.notes: The issue stayed open after the merge. Streaming would let `tar ... | gdrive files upload` start sending immediately instead of first writing the whole archive to /tmp. That part is M effort, because google-apis-common's resumable uploader needs a known content length.

issues.title: Creation  of the app in development? (something change)
issues.still_relevant_reason: The user is stuck on Google's unverified-app/consent warning; the 'Continue' link pointing to accounts.google.com/# is Google's UI, not gdrive's. The docs never explain this screen (docs/create_google_api_credentials.md), and Testing-mode apps also need the user added as a test user (steps 16-17).
issues.recommendation: Cover this in the rewritten credentials guide (screenshot of 'Google hasn't verified this app' -> Advanced -> 'Go to <app> (unsafe)'), then close as support.
issues.notes: No replies. It can't be reproduced from gdrive's side.

issues.title: Getting error when downloading large files
issues.still_relevant_reason: Any error while reading the response body aborts the download and leaves a `.incomplete` file (src/files/download.rs:309-312). download_file makes a single GET with no retry, no backoff and no Range resume (src/files/download.rs:189-200), unlike uploads (src/common/delegate.rs). The client negotiates HTTP/2 (src/hub.rs:36-37), and Google resets long-lived h2 streams and connections. Neither fork adds download retries.
issues.recommendation: Wrap media downloads in a retry loop with exponential backoff for transient errors (h2 RST_STREAM/GOAWAY, connection reset, 5xx, 429). Resume from the .incomplete file's length with an HTTP Range header and verify the MD5 at the end. Offer --http1 and consider HTTP/1.1 for media. In recursive mode, continue past per-file errors and print a summary.
issues.notes: #78 has the same root cause (h2 GOAWAY max_age during long recursive downloads). Download retry should land before parallel downloads (PR #68, fork:toutizes), because more concurrent streams mean more resets. Pairs with #12.

issues.title: Add the ability to configure a proxy server
issues.still_relevant_reason: There is no proxy support anywhere. hub.rs builds a plain HttpsConnector client (src/hub.rs:33-40) and the authenticator uses yup-oauth2's default client (src/hub.rs:64-71), so http_proxy, https_proxy, ALL_PROXY and the Windows system proxy are all ignored (gdrive2 honored them). Neither fork adds proxy support; PR #141 does, using hyper-proxy on hyper 0.14.
issues.recommendation: Implement env and system proxy support (HTTP CONNECT and SOCKS5, NO_PROXY, proxy auth) on the modern stack via the hyper-util client-proxy feature (Matcher::from_env/from_system, Tunnel, SocksV5). Use one shared client for both DriveHub and the OAuth authenticator, and add a --proxy flag/config override. Use PR #141 only as a reference, since hyper-proxy is tied to hyper 0.14.
issues.notes: Recurring demand across #21, #26, #59 and #74, mostly from users behind corporate proxies or the GFW. The comment shows rclone honoring the same env vars.

issues.title: `files list` replacing part of long file names with '...'
issues.still_relevant_reason: Implemented in 3.7.0: --full-name (main.rs:148-150; list.rs:242-252 truncates only when truncate_name), --skip-header and --field-separator (main.rs:144-154), and recursive download skips files whose local md5 matches (download.rs:166-168).
issues.recommendation: Nothing to do. The remaining gap, a literal tab separator, is tracked in #52 (PR #113).
issues.notes: Names are still truncated by default (41 chars with a U+2026 ellipsis, list.rs:247,269). Consider turning truncation off automatically when stdout is not a TTY.

issues.title: Update spreadsheet with csv file?
issues.still_relevant_reason: You cannot append a CSV to an existing Sheet. `files update <sheet_id> new.csv` replaces the sheet content in place through a resumable upload (update.rs:96-108); #31 confirms this works. Formatting is not kept and nothing is appended.
issues.recommendation: Answer and close. `gdrive files update <sheet_id> new.csv` replaces the content and keeps the id and sharing. Appending rows needs the Sheets API (spreadsheets.values.append), which is out of scope for a Drive CLI. Add a docs FAQ line.
issues.notes: Side effect: update also renames the remote file to the local basename (update.rs:92-94), so the Sheet would be renamed to 'new.csv'. Consider keeping the remote name unless --name is given.

issues.title: Why rewrite from Go to Rust?
issues.still_relevant_reason: A question about why the project moved to Rust. The author answered it (to gain Rust experience). Nothing in the code to change.
issues.recommendation: No action. Already closed.

issues.title: Unable to add account
issues.still_relevant_reason: The only auth path is a loopback redirect on the fixed port 8085 (hub.rs:64-71). There is no way to paste the code or URL by hand, so a browser on another machine gets '127.0.0.1 refused'. The README offers only add-locally plus account export/import.
issues.recommendation: Add a headless `account add --manual` flow. Use yup-oauth2 InstalledFlowReturnMethod::Interactive with InstalledFlowDelegate::redirect_uri() overridden to http://127.0.0.1:8085, and have the user paste the redirected URL (parse code=). Also document the ssh -L tunnel (adopt PR #132) and the curl-the-redirect trick (#161).
issues.notes: In yup-oauth2 12.1.2 the Interactive path propagates the delegate result (installed.rs:144-169) and uses delegate.redirect_uri() for both the auth URL and the token exchange (installed.rs:217-218, 234-237), so no listener is needed and the flow stays within Google's loopback-only policy (OOB was removed). Device flow is not an option because Google does not allow the full drive scope on it. The OOB redirect_uris value in hub.rs:83 is a dead placeholder. The 'command not found' sub-question was a user PATH problem, answered in the thread.

issues.title: Failed to update/import large csv file
issues.still_relevant_reason: update already uses a resumable upload for any non-empty file (update.rs:107-108), and upload uses one for files larger than the chunk size (upload.rs:242-246). The 413 uploadTooLarge comes from Google's size limit for converting a 220 MB CSV into a Google Sheet. The reporter closed the issue.
issues.recommendation: No code change. Optionally map 413 uploadTooLarge during a conversion to a hint: 'too large to convert to Google Sheets; upload without conversion'.
issues.notes: Flagged as speed-related only because it asks about resumable uploads, which already exist. The thread shows that `files update <sheet_id> file.csv` updates a Sheet in place, which answers #28.

issues.title: Remote server
issues.still_relevant_reason: When Google rejects the refresh token (it expires after 7 days on a Testing consent screen, or was revoked), yup-oauth2 silently falls back to the interactive installed flow (8.1.0 authenticator.rs:143-150; 12.1.2 authenticator.rs:147-155). That flow binds 127.0.0.1:8085 (hub.rs:64-71) and waits forever, so the next cron run fails with 'Address in use (os error 98)'. In HTTP-redirect mode yup-oauth2 ignores the delegate's result (installed.rs:201-205), so the current delegate (hub.rs:105-111) cannot abort.
issues.recommendation: Fail fast when not interactive. If stdin is not a terminal (or --non-interactive / GDRIVE_NONINTERACTIVE is set), return a clear error instead of starting the listener: 're-authorize with gdrive account add; publish the consent screen to Production to avoid the 7-day expiry'. Use the Interactive return method, whose delegate error propagates, or wrap token() in a timeout. Bind an ephemeral port (HTTPRedirect) so a stuck instance cannot block the next run.
issues.notes: Related: #147 (non-interactive mode) and #22 (weekly re-auth). Workaround today: kill the stuck gdrive process, then re-add or re-import the account. Both forks still use HTTPPortRedirect(8085) (dodomorandi hub.rs:62, toutizes hub.rs:66).

issues.title: file id and resource key
issues.still_relevant_reason: The source has no resource-key support (no resourceKey or X-Goog-Drive-Resource-Keys in src or either fork). files.get is called with the bare id (download.rs:189-200), and every command needs a configured account (hub_helper.rs:11-21).
issues.recommendation: Accept Drive URLs as file arguments: parse /d/<id>, ?id=, /folders/<id> and resourcekey=. Send the `X-Goog-Drive-Resource-Keys: <id>/<key>` header. google-drive3 call builders only offer .param() and cannot add headers, so do the media GET as a raw request using the hub's token. Account-less download is covered by #50.
issues.notes: Resource keys only matter for link-shared items from before Google's 2021 security update that the user has never opened. URL parsing on its own is a small win for every command.

issues.title: App registration requires varification by Google
issues.still_relevant_reason: docs/create_google_api_credentials.md says to publish the app (steps 26-28) but never explains the 'Google hasn't verified this app' warning or the verification notice. Its click-by-click steps also predate Google moving the consent screen into the Google Auth Platform pages (Branding, Audience, Data access, Clients).
issues.recommendation: Rewrite the credentials guide for the current Google Auth Platform UI. Cover: External audience plus In production (unverified is fine for personal use and avoids the 7-day refresh expiry), clicking through 'Advanced > Go to <app> (unsafe)', and why verification is not needed. Fold in PR #96 (inline screenshots) and PR #137 (typo fix).
issues.notes: Testing-mode refresh tokens expire after 7 days, which is the root cause of #22, #33 and #51. The thread's warning that an unpublished key 'becomes invalid after a week' is correct.

issues.title: Your client has taken too long to issue its request.
issues.still_relevant_reason: should_retry only retries 5xx and 429 (delegate.rs:119-121), so a 408 Request Timeout on a chunk aborts the whole upload (http_failure, delegate.rs:97-116). 403 rateLimitExceeded and userRateLimitExceeded are not retried either. The Backoff attempt counter is never reset after a successful chunk (delegate.rs:157-163). After a few transient errors, every later retry waits max_sleep (60 s), and the retry budget is shared across the whole file (100000 for upload, upload.rs:43; 20 for update, update.rs:36).
issues.recommendation: Retry 408 and the 403 rate-limit reasons (parse error.errors[].reason). Reset the backoff after each committed chunk (detect progress in cancel_chunk_upload). Show retries in normal output, not only with --print-chunk-errors. Advise --chunk-size 8 or 16 on slow uplinks.
issues.notes: Chunk retries in a resumable upload go through the delegate (google-apis fork drive3 client.rs:727-742), so fixing the delegate is enough. dodomorandi has the same should_retry and an iterator backoff that never resets (delegate.rs:116-118, 137-160). Downloads have no retry at all (see #56).

issues.title: Please support Google Application Default Credentials
issues.still_relevant_reason: Only the installed OAuth flow exists (hub.rs:56-75, hub_helper.rs:11-21). There is no --access-token (v2 had one) and no GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS or gcloud ADC support. The dependencies already cover it: google-apis-common 8 implements GetToken for String (auth.rs:104-107), DriveHub::new accepts any GetToken (google-drive3 7 api.rs:177), and yup-oauth2 12 ships ApplicationDefaultCredentials, AuthorizedUser, AccessToken, ExternalAccount and ServiceAccountImpersonation authenticators (authenticator.rs:316-497).
issues.recommendation: Add pluggable auth backends together with #49: a global --access-token / GDRIVE_ACCESS_TOKEN (raw bearer token, v2 parity); --credentials <json> or GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS that auto-detects service_account, authorized_user or external_account JSON; and a GCE metadata fallback. Have Hub hold a Box<dyn GetToken> instead of the concrete Authenticator (hub.rs:21,46).
issues.notes: Related to #49 (implement both as one work item). gcloud's own client may be refused for Drive scopes on ADC login, so users might need `gcloud auth application-default login --client-id-file=...`; document it. ExternalAccount (workload identity federation) allows keyless CI such as GitHub Actions OIDC. account add calls auth.token() directly (account/add.rs:25-30) and needs the same abstraction.

issues.title: Thanks

issues.recommendation: Close. Optionally link community guides from the docs.

issues.title: 'files update' vagueness (migrated from v2)
issues.still_relevant_reason: files update takes one file (main.rs:218-238; File::open in file_helper.rs:14-19) and writes a new revision of a single file id. There is no sync (v2's sync was dropped). Passing a directory gives a raw OS error on Windows (os error 5). On Linux File::open succeeds on a directory and the read fails later in the resumable helper's read_to_end().unwrap() (google-apis fork drive3 client.rs:686); this is probably a panic (inferred, not run).
issues.recommendation: Reject directories in `files update` with a clear message pointing to `upload --recursive` or a future sync command. Document what update does: new revision, same id, about 30-day version retention. Track folder sync in #16, #69 and #84, starting from toutizes' upload --overwrite/--sync.
issues.notes: update also renames the remote file to the local basename (update.rs:92-94); for stdin input that becomes the temp-file name. The user's second comment shows the id was mangled by brackets they typed.

issues.title: Unknown file type
issues.still_relevant_reason: FileTree::from_path aborts the whole upload on any entry that is neither is_dir() nor is_file() (file_tree.rs:121-133). The branch meant to catch symlinks repeats `path.is_file()` (file_tree.rs:129), so it never fires. Dangling symlinks, sockets and FIFOs all produce 'Unknown file type' and stop the upload.
issues.recommendation: Skip dangling symlinks and special files with a warning instead of aborting, add --follow-symlinks / --skip-symlinks, and fix the duplicated is_file() check. toutizes already skips per item with an error (upload.rs:129-137). dodomorandi fixes the check (file_tree.rs:105) but still aborts.
issues.notes: is_dir() and is_file() follow symlinks, so valid symlinks are uploaded as their targets; only dangling links reach this branch. The reporter's 'test.sh' was most likely a dangling symlink.

issues.title: "Error: Account '[ACCOUNT_NAME]' not found"
issues.still_relevant_reason: Export compares the name exactly against directories in ~/.config/gdrive3 that contain tokens.json (app_config.rs:37-52, export.rs:57-63). `account current` prints the name from account.json without that check (current.rs:7-14). Most likely user error (brackets, or a different HOME under sudo). However, an account whose tokens.json is missing shows up in `current` and is reported 'not found' by export.
issues.recommendation: Make `account export` default to the current account when no name is given, and list the available accounts in the not-found error. Warn in `account current` when the account has no tokens.json.

issues.title: Progress bar during download or upload
issues.still_relevant_reason: Download only prints 'Downloading <name>' (download.rs:125,174) and streams chunks with no feedback (download.rs:309-312). Upload prints 'Uploading' (upload.rs:97), with optional per-chunk lines via --print-chunk-info (delegate.rs:46-66). There is no byte counter, speed or ETA anywhere. Neither fork adds one; toutizes only prints a final bandwidth summary (toutizes download.rs:80).
issues.recommendation: Add indicatif progress bars on stderr, turned off when stderr is not a TTY or with --quiet, --print-only-id or --stdout. Show per-file bytes, speed and ETA for downloads (wrap the body stream; size comes from file.size), one overall bar for recursive operations (tree_info.total_file_size), and chunk-level upload progress via Delegate::cancel_chunk_upload. Design it together with the parallel transfer engine (MultiProgress).
issues.notes: Byte-level upload progress cannot come from a reader wrapper: google-apis-common reads each chunk fully into memory before sending it (8.0.0 lib.rs:685-687; same in the fork), and files at or below the chunk size go in one multipart request. Finer upload progress needs smaller chunks or our own streaming resumable uploader, which a speed-focused fork may want anyway. PR #157 tracks progress only inside its TUI. The reporter closed the issue after switching to gdown, but with 19 +1 it is among the most-demanded items in the tracker; duplicate #12 adds 5 more.

issues.title: Can't delete files
issues.still_relevant_reason: Every command takes a file id by design. `files delete` passes its argument straight to files.get and files.delete (delete.rs:14-29), so a name returns 404. Upstream has no name or path resolution.
issues.recommendation: Add one resolver for all file arguments (id, Drive URL, or /path/in/drive) by porting toutizes' drive_names::resolve. Error out when several files share the name. Make the 404 message say 'expected a file id'.
issues.notes: toutizes only partly covers this: its resolver (common/drive_names.rs:19) is used for download and upload, but delete is still id-only. Related: #14 (delete several files) and #117 (filter by name).

issues.title: Add support for SSLKEYLOGFILE (for rustls)
issues.still_relevant_reason: The connector is built with HttpsConnectorBuilder::with_native_roots() (hub.rs:33-38) without a custom rustls ClientConfig, so key_log is never set. Neither fork changes this (dodomorandi hub.rs:22-30).
issues.recommendation: During the hyper-rustls 0.27 migration, build the rustls ClientConfig explicitly and set key_log = Arc::new(rustls::KeyLogFile::new()), which honours SSLKEYLOGFILE. Possibly put it behind a debug flag.
issues.notes: A debugging aid only. Marked as modernization because it belongs to the TLS connector rewrite.

issues.title: Command 'gdrive' not found
issues.still_relevant_reason: A PATH and installation mix-up (the user solved it), followed by the remote-browser '127.0.0.1 refused to connect' problem that #30 already covers.
issues.recommendation: Close. Covered by the install docs (#6) and the headless-auth work in #30.

issues.title: Great work, a bit unsure about what the different commands do and about wildcards?
issues.still_relevant_reason: `files upload` takes a single optional path (main.rs:184-186), so a shell-expanded wildcard fails with a clap 'unexpected argument' error. There is no multi-file upload and no move (delete local after upload). The thread's suggestion `gdrive upload $(ls ...)` would not work either.
issues.recommendation: Accept several paths in `files upload` (Vec<PathBuf>; the shell does the globbing) and add --delete-after or --move (#93). This also feeds the parallel upload queue.
issues.notes: Related: #93 (delete local file after upload) and #14 (delete several files).

issues.title: Support service account credentials
issues.still_relevant_reason: There is no service-account support: Auth::new always builds an InstalledFlowAuthenticator (hub.rs:56-75), and accounts can only be created through the interactive `account add` (account/add.rs:9-60). The dependencies already provide it: yup-oauth2 8.1.0 (upstream lock) and 12.1.2 both ship ServiceAccountAuthenticator (12.1.2 authenticator.rs:267-293), with .subject() for domain-wide delegation (authenticator.rs:739-747), and DriveHub accepts any GetToken.
issues.recommendation: Add `gdrive account add --service-account <key.json> [--subject user@domain]`: store the key in the account dir and name the account after client_email or the subject. Add a one-shot --service-account / GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS mode for CI. Build the authenticator with ServiceAccountAuthenticator::with_client(key, client) and persist its tokens. Enable yup-oauth2's service-account feature (dodomorandi sets default-features = false, which turns it off; google-drive3 7 offers the yup-oauth2-service-account feature).
issues.notes: With 23 +1 this is the most-demanded open issue. Service accounts avoid the consent screen, the 7-day expiry and the loopback redirect (#30/#33/#35). Caveats to document: (1) a service account sees only its own empty My Drive plus items shared with it, so the default 'root' in parents listing is useless; point users to sharedWithMe or --drive. (2) Google rejects uploads owned by a service account outside shared drives with 'Service Accounts do not have storage quota' (verify the current wording), so uploads need a Shared Drive or domain-wide delegation, which is Workspace-only. v2 had --service-account <file> relative to the config dir; keep that flag name. Implement together with #37 (one auth-backend abstraction).

issues.title: Ability to download files without an account
issues.still_relevant_reason: Every command needs a configured account (hub_helper.rs:11-21 calls AppConfig::load_current_account). There is no anonymous or API-key mode. google-apis-common 8 provides NoToken (auth.rs:115-118) and the call builders have .param("key", ...), so public files could be fetched without OAuth.
issues.recommendation: Add `files download --public`, or fall back to it when no account exists. For 'anyone with the link' files, use the Drive API with an API key (GDRIVE_API_KEY plus NoToken), or the drive.usercontent.google.com download endpoint as gdown does; that endpoint is undocumented and may break, and needs handling of the virus-scan confirm page. Also document the Firefox 'Something went wrong' workaround (use a Chromium-based browser for the consent step).
issues.notes: Related: #34 (resource keys) and #111 (README on public downloads). v2's 'no sign-in' really came from its built-in OAuth client, which Google later blocked. A shared built-in client is not an option for the fork, because the restricted drive scope would need verification.

issues.title: Failed to upload file: Token retrieval failed
issues.still_relevant_reason: The same 'Address in use (os error 98)' failure after about 6 days as #33: the refresh token expired (Testing consent screen) and the interactive flow's listener was left running. The reporter fixed it by recreating the tokens on a PC and copying them over.
issues.recommendation: Close as a duplicate of #33 and fix it there (fail fast, ephemeral port, docs on publishing to Production).

issues.title: files list field separator does not allow tab character
issues.still_relevant_reason: table::write always sends rows through TabWriter (table.rs:26-41), which turns literal tab separators into padded spaces. Any other separator passes through unchanged, so tab is the only one that cannot be used. This affects files list, drives list and permissions list.
issues.recommendation: Adopt the --tsv idea from PR #113 but make it general: skip TabWriter when --field-separator is given explicitly or stdout is not a TTY, and add --json output for scripts, since names can contain tabs or newlines.
issues.notes: PR #113 (+47/-8) adds a tsv flag to DisplayConfig for all three list commands. It does not escape tabs or newlines inside names.

issues.title: Error: Filename too long (os error 36) - Breaks Recursive Download
issues.still_relevant_reason: Drive names become local file names verbatim (download.rs:162-175; file_tree_drive.rs:97-131), with no length or character sanitizing. The temp file uses with_extension("incomplete") (download.rs:302), which replaces the extension and can push a name near 255 bytes over NAME_MAX even when the final name fits. Any per-file error aborts the whole recursive download through `?` (download.rs:170-175).
issues.recommendation: Sanitize local names: truncate to 255 bytes keeping the extension, and replace '/' and Windows-reserved characters (reuse sanitize_filename from serebrov's PR #164 branch). Continue past per-file errors, then print an error summary and exit non-zero, following toutizes' per-task Failed status. Add --fail-fast to keep the old behaviour.
issues.notes: PR #164 was closed (opened by accident), but its branch has sanitize_filename and a warnings list. Use an appended suffix or a unique temp file instead of with_extension: same-stem files (a.pdf and a.docx) both map to 'a.incomplete', which becomes a race once downloads run in parallel (toutizes disk_item.rs:181 has the same problem). Related: #19 (slash in name) and #152 (a 1.2 TB transfer aborted by one infected file). vlazic's commit d41b897 (outside this repo) logs and continues.

issues.title: Upload single file
issues.still_relevant_reason: Upload always creates a new file (files.create in upload.rs:213-249), and Drive allows duplicate names. Replacing a file requires its id and `files update`. Upload has no --overwrite or --skip-existing.
issues.recommendation: Adopt toutizes' upload semantics: --overwrite updates the same-name file in the target folder and skips it when the md5 matches, it errors when several files share the name, and --skip-existing skips. Keep the default backward compatible (always create) or make the change explicit.
issues.notes: toutizes makes Skip the default when a same-name file exists (upload.rs:247-253), a behaviour change to decide deliberately. Part of the sync theme (#16, #69, #84).

issues.title: Adding option --skip
issues.still_relevant_reason: There is no --skip flag. `--recursive --overwrite` already skips files whose local md5 matches (download.rs:166-168; documented in #152), but without --overwrite an existing root folder aborts the run (download.rs:82, 334-357). Interrupted files are not resumed: the temp file restarts from 0 (download.rs:296-319). Downloads have no retry or backoff at all (download.rs:170-175, 309-311). The identical-file check hashes every local file even when sizes differ (download.rs:406-422).
issues.recommendation: Add --skip-existing (name and size check, md5 optional) and make --overwrite compare size before md5. Retry downloads with exponential backoff on stream, 5xx and 429 errors. Resume .incomplete files with HTTP Range requests. These are core to fast, restartable bulk downloads.
issues.notes: The reported 'stream error received: unexpected internal error' is an HTTP/2 RST_STREAM from Google that a retry would absorb. toutizes skips existing files per file and downloads in parallel. It has a bug, though: download.rs:207-212 prints 'file exists, skipped.' under Abort, then falls through and re-downloads when the md5 differs.

issues.title: List files limitation
issues.still_relevant_reason: Fixed by PR #104 (upstream commit ca21e02, released in 3.9.1): list() no longer caps max_files at MAX_PAGE_SIZE, and list_files follows nextPageToken until --max is reached (list.rs:81-126). The issue is still open upstream.
issues.recommendation: Close as fixed in 3.9.1. Consider --max 0 meaning unlimited, and printing each page as it arrives instead of collecting all pages in memory.
issues.notes: 1000 is the Drive API's maximum page size for files.list. The fields list is already restricted (list.rs:105-108).

issues.title: "The Trust Settings Record was corrupted." error on macOS... and solution.
issues.still_relevant_reason: Upstream pins hyper-rustls 0.23.2 / rustls-native-certs 0.6.2 (Cargo.lock); hub.rs:33-34 calls with_native_roots(), which does load_native_certs().expect("could not load platform certs") (hyper-rustls-0.23.2/src/config.rs:31), so one bad macOS trust-settings record panics the whole program. Closed by the reporter with an external workaround, not a code fix.
issues.recommendation: Fixed by the dependency upgrade: hyper-rustls 0.27 returns an io::Result from with_native_roots and fails only when zero roots load, and rustls-native-certs 0.8 macos.rs skips untrusted certs and keeps going. Take dodomorandi's hub.rs create_connector() (with_native_roots()? and no panic), and print a clear error naming the bad certificate store.
issues.notes: Same panic as #112 (Linux NotFound and macOS -25262). Consider rustls-platform-verifier, with webpki-roots as a fallback, so it also covers #80.

issues.title: Error adding account
issues.still_relevant_reason: The browser step succeeds, then the token exchange to oauth2.googleapis.com times out (os error 60). The user is behind the GFW and gdrive has no proxy support: hub.rs:33-40 builds a plain HttpsConnector, and yup-oauth2 8.1 builds its own direct connector. HTTP(S)_PROXY is ignored, as the comments confirm.
issues.recommendation: Close as a duplicate of the proxy feature (#26/#74). Fixed once env-proxy support covers both the DriveHub client and the OAuth token client.
issues.notes: PR #141 lists 'fix #59'. Workarounds from the comments: proxychains (macOS), tun2proxy (#74).

issues.title: Access blocked: project-367116221053’s request is invalid
issues.still_relevant_reason: Project 367116221053 is the built-in OAuth client of the old prasmussen/gdrive v2 (handlers_drive.go:17 ClientId=367116221053-...), which used the OOB flow (redirect_uri=urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob) that Google shut down. gdrive3 asks users for their own client and uses loopback redirect InstalledFlowReturnMethod::HTTPPortRedirect(8085) (hub.rs:64-66), so this error cannot come from v3.
issues.recommendation: Close as not-actionable: the user is running gdrive v2. Add a README FAQ line saying v2's OOB login no longer works and v3 needs your own OAuth client. Also delete the dead OOB redirect_uris entry at hub.rs:83 so nobody thinks OOB is still used.
issues.notes: #99 comment ('the old one ... error 400') is the same v2 OOB failure. The last comment (works from CLI but not from a script) points to a different, older binary on PATH.

issues.title: a way to list mime types for Google docs?
issues.still_relevant_reason: Already possible: 'gdrive files info <id>' prints a Mime field (info.rs:79-82). The export error already lists the allowed extensions (export.rs:125-135). There is still no way to see the supported export formats before exporting.
issues.recommendation: Answer with 'files info <id>'. Optionally have 'files info' print 'Export formats: ...' for Google Docs files, using DocType::supported_export_types (drive_file.rs:127). Merge with the #73 list improvement.
issues.notes: Related to #73. Export only handles Document/Spreadsheet/Presentation (drive_file.rs:99-104); Drawings/Forms/Apps Script cannot be exported.

issues.title: Suggestion: Copy usage over from prasmussen/gdrive
issues.still_relevant_reason: Partly done: PR #66 (merged 2023-07-16) added docs/basic_usage.md, but it only covers list/info/download/export and the README has no command reference. There is no v2-to-v3 migration guide either ('sync' is gone, '-p' is now '--parent', etc.).
issues.recommendation: Generate a full command reference from clap (clap_mangen and/or clap-markdown in CI) and add a short v2-to-v3 migration table covering sync, -p/--parent, the root alias and the --skip equivalent. Merge PR #138's basic_usage fix.
issues.notes: Overlaps #106 (Insufficient Documentation) and #48. Missing 'sync' is the #84/#16 feature gap.

issues.title: Add binary for arm64
issues.still_relevant_reason: Releases ship only x64 builds (3.9.1 assets: gdrive_linux-x64, gdrive_macos-x64, gdrive_windows-x64). .github/workflows/release_linux.yaml builds x86_64-unknown-linux-musl via clux/muslrust only. Also, release_macos.yaml uses macos-latest, which is now an arm64 runner, so a rebuild today would upload an arm64 binary named 'macos-x64'.
issues.recommendation: Replace the three release workflows with one matrix release (houseabsolute/actions-rust-cross or cargo-zigbuild) for linux x86_64/aarch64/armv7 musl, macOS x86_64+arm64 (or universal) and Windows x64(+arm64), uploaded with softprops/action-gh-release. Take PR #130's target list (aarch64-musl, armv7-musleabihf, arm-musleabi, macOS arm) as the starting point.
issues.notes: The comment about cargo failing with 'Permission denied' on ~/.cargo/git is a local permissions problem from the git dependency, which goes away once google-drive3 comes from crates.io (dodomorandi). #135's 'cannot execute: required file not found' shows why static musl ARM builds matter.

issues.title: Downloading Everything from Google Drive at Once
issues.still_relevant_reason: 'gdrive files download --recursive root' should work: get_file accepts the Drive 'root' alias (info.rs:35-49) and download_directory walks it (download.rs:134-187). But Google Docs/Sheets/Slides are silently skipped (file_tree_drive.rs:130-132), 'Shared with me' items are not included, downloads run one at a time, and none of this is documented.
issues.recommendation: Document 'gdrive files download --recursive root --destination DIR' (and mention Google Takeout). Take PR #162 so recursive downloads export Docs/Sheets/Slides instead of skipping them, and add parallel download (PR #68 / toutizes TaskManager) so full-drive backups are fast.
issues.notes: The 'root' alias path was checked against the code but not run against a live account. A full-drive backup is the main use case for parallel download, so transfer_speed=true.

issues.title: How could I overwrite a file previously upload only specifiying its name?
issues.still_relevant_reason: Upload always creates a new file (upload.rs:213-249, files().create). 'files update' needs a file id (main.rs:217-240) and there is no name/path lookup or replace-if-exists option. The workaround is to capture the id with --print-only-id, or to look it up with 'files list --query "name='x' and 'PARENT' in parents"'.
issues.recommendation: Add 'upload --overwrite' (replace a same-named file in the target folder via files.update so version history is kept; skip if the md5 matches) and accept Drive paths as targets. Port toutizes' ExistingDriveFileAction::Replace and drive_names.rs path resolution, and error out when a name matches more than one file.
issues.notes: Same code path as #84/#69 (sync). Drive allows duplicate names, so detect ambiguity, as toutizes does.

issues.title: recursive update
issues.still_relevant_reason: 'files update' takes one file id and has no --recursive (main.rs:217-240). Recursive upload always creates new folders (main.rs:196 help text; upload.rs:136-199 mkdir for every folder). Updating an existing remote tree in place is impossible.
issues.recommendation: Track under #84 (sync/skip). Implement 'upload --recursive --overwrite' that reuses existing remote folders by name and updates only changed files (toutizes do_update_file + md5 match), then close this as a duplicate.
issues.notes: Skipping unchanged files avoids re-uploading, which is why transfer_speed=true.

issues.title: Save config files in a global place for all users (Windows)
issues.still_relevant_reason: The config dir is hardcoded to home_dir()/.config/gdrive3 (app_config.rs:10-11,159-165), with no env var, flag or XDG_CONFIG_HOME support (no std::env usage in src/). Windows SYSTEM/services and Unix daemons cannot point gdrive at a shared config.
issues.recommendation: Add a GDRIVE_CONFIG_DIR env var and a global --config-dir flag, and respect XDG_CONFIG_HOME on Unix, keeping ~/.config/gdrive3 as the default for compatibility. Document the SYSTEM workaround (%SystemRoot%\System32\config\systemprofile).
issues.notes: Would also cover #88. Neither fork changed default_base_path (dodomorandi app_config.rs:244-250).

issues.title: Cannot access Google drive
issues.still_relevant_reason: The OAuth loopback server binds only 127.0.0.1:8085 (hub.rs:66; yup-oauth2 installed.rs:287). On a remote or headless box (or WSL), the browser redirect to 127.0.0.1 is refused. The README export/import workaround exists (README.md:44-51), but there is no in-tool headless flow.
issues.recommendation: Add 'account add --manual': print the URL, let the user paste the full redirected http://127.0.0.1:8085/?code=... URL (or just the code), and exchange it, using yup-oauth2 Interactive return with a custom redirect_uri. Also make the port/bind configurable. Merge PR #132's ssh -L 8085 tunnel docs and keep export/import documented.
issues.notes: Related: #33, #125 (add auth code manually, 5 reactions), #139, #161 (curl the redirect URL on the server). Google removed OOB, so loopback plus manual paste is the only headless option for the full drive scope; device flow does not allow the drive scope.

issues.title: How do I set up multiple gdrive accounts?
issues.still_relevant_reason: Supported: run 'account add' again, then 'account list' / 'account switch <name>' (main.rs:60-94; app_config.rs:33-52). But the account is a global 'current' setting in account.json, and there is no per-command account override, so concurrent scripts on different accounts race.
issues.recommendation: Document the add/list/switch workflow in the README. Add a global '--account <name>' flag / GDRIVE_ACCOUNT env var read by hub_helper::get_hub (hub_helper.rs:11-21) so scripts don't need to switch.
issues.notes: Pairs with #70 (--config-dir).

issues.title: How to differentiate Sheets from Docs when using list?
issues.still_relevant_reason: simplified_file_type (list.rs:230-240) maps every Google-native type to 'document', although mimeType is already fetched (list.rs:107). Workaround: --query "mimeType='application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet'". Both forks keep the same 'document' mapping.
issues.recommendation: Show the specific kind (document/spreadsheet/presentation/form/drawing) in the Type column, or add an optional Mime column (--show-mime). Consider a machine-readable output mode (--json) for scripts like the one described.
issues.notes: Same need as #61. Recursive export with formats chosen per type is PR #162.

issues.title: How to use proxy?
issues.still_relevant_reason: No proxy support: hub.rs:33-40 uses a bare HttpsConnector, and yup-oauth2 8.1 builds its own direct client (authenticator.rs:930-947). HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY are ignored, unlike gdrive2. Neither fork adds it.
issues.recommendation: Add env-proxy support (HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY, socks5 via ALL_PROXY) on the upgraded stack using hyper-util's client::proxy::matcher::Matcher::from_env plus connect::proxy::{Tunnel,SocksV5} (hyper-util 0.1.20). Use the same connector for DriveHub and yup-oauth2 (with_client, as dodomorandi does). Port PR #141's idea, not its code: it uses hyper-proxy 0.9, which only works with hyper 0.14.
issues.notes: Canonical issue is #26 (4 reactions). Also fixes #59 and #21 per PR #141. Workarounds: proxychains, tun2proxy.

issues.title: Option to store credentials using an external tool, such as `pass`
issues.still_relevant_reason: Secrets go in plaintext secret.json (app_config.rs:101-114, chmod 600 on Unix only), and tokens are persisted by yup-oauth2 persist_tokens_to_disk (hub.rs:68). There is no external or keyring storage.
issues.recommendation: Low priority. If implemented, add a custom yup-oauth2 TokenStorage (with_storage) backed by the OS keyring (keyring crate) or by user-configured '*_command' hooks, behind an opt-in setting.

issues.title: Shell completions
issues.still_relevant_reason: No completion support: the CLI is clap 4 derive (main.rs:20-25), but there is no clap_complete dependency (Cargo.toml) and no completions subcommand. Neither fork adds one.
issues.recommendation: Add 'gdrive completions <bash|zsh|fish|powershell|elvish>' via clap_complete (plus a man page via clap_mangen) and include the generated files in release archives.
issues.notes: Cheap and makes a good first PR for the fork.

issues.title: Error: Failed to download file: http2 error: connection error received: not a result of an error (b"max_age")
issues.still_relevant_reason: Google's frontend sends an HTTP/2 GOAWAY(NO_ERROR, 'max_age') on long-lived connections (hub.rs:37 enable_http2; hyper 0.14.23/h2 0.3.15). Downloads have no retry or resume at all: download_file (download.rs:189-200) and save_body_to_file abort on the first error, so a day-long recursive download dies. Uploads, by contrast, retry up to 100000 times (upload.rs:43).
issues.recommendation: Add download retries with exponential backoff that resume with an HTTP Range header from the bytes already written, and treat h2 GOAWAY/connection-reset/5xx/429 as retryable. Upgrade hyper/h2 (dodomorandi). Consider a '--http1' option or an HTTP/1.1 connection pool for parallel bulk transfers.
issues.notes: The commenter fixed it by removing enable_http2 (hub.rs:37). Neither fork retries downloads (grep shows backoff only in upload/update). Retries plus Range resume matter for both reliability and throughput.

issues.title: Does not compile on ARM
issues.still_relevant_reason: This is an old-rustc problem, not an ARM one. The elided lifetime in 'const IMPORT_EXTENSION_MAP: &[(FileExtension, DocType)]' (drive_file.rs:64) fails on rustc 1.62.1 but compiles on 1.74 and on 1.99.1: upstream builds cleanly per build_log.txt, and a minimal repro compiles with no warning on 1.99.1.
issues.recommendation: Apply the trivial '&'static' fix (PR #127), or take dodomorandi's array const. Declare 'rust-version' (MSRV) in Cargo.toml and check it in CI so old distro toolchains get a clear message.
issues.notes: #101 asks for this fix together with ARM releases (#63). #131 is a separate RPi toolchain problem.

issues.title: Unknown issuer error upon adding account.
issues.still_relevant_reason: TLS trust comes only from the OS root store via rustls-native-certs (hub.rs:34 with_native_roots; yup-oauth2 8.1 likewise). On Windows, roots that were never installed in the store (Windows installs roots on demand) or TLS-inspecting corporate proxies/antivirus cause UnknownIssuer. dodomorandi still uses with_native_roots, so the problem remains there.
issues.recommendation: During the TLS dependency upgrade, switch to rustls-platform-verifier (uses the OS verifier, including Windows CryptoAPI root fetching and enterprise roots), with webpki-roots as an optional fallback. Allow an extra CA bundle via SSL_CERT_FILE.
issues.notes: Same TLS-root family as #58/#112. Fix all three in one change.

issues.title: Wrong link for query params in help

issues.title: Lock Google Drive access to a single directory?
issues.still_relevant_reason: OAuth cannot be limited to one folder. gdrive also hardcodes the full 'drive' scope plus drive.metadata.readonly at login (account/add.rs:25-28), and every call adds Scope::Full (e.g. list.rs:102, upload.rs:238). The narrower drive.file scope (only files the app created or opened) cannot be chosen.
issues.recommendation: Document that per-folder restriction is impossible. Add an opt-in 'account add --scope file' (drive.file) mode and thread the stored scope through all requests instead of hardcoded Scope::Full. Note: 'drive' is a Google restricted scope (verification/CASA for public apps), while drive.file is non-sensitive, which also eases the 'needs verification' issues.
issues.notes: Google-auth-policy item. With drive.file, list/download only see files gdrive itself created, so document that clearly. The drive.metadata.readonly scope is redundant next to drive.

issues.title: Rsync-style behavior
issues.still_relevant_reason: Upload has no --skip/--sync: upload_directory always creates new folders and re-uploads everything (upload.rs:115-211). Download is partly there: 'download --recursive --overwrite' already skips files whose local md5 matches (download.rs:166-168, local_file_is_identical download.rs:406), but this is undocumented (#152) and nothing is deleted or exported.
issues.recommendation: Implement sync semantics for both directions: '--skip-existing' (md5/size compare), '--sync' (also delete extras, with a --dry-run), and reuse of existing remote folders by name. Port toutizes' design (upload/download --overwrite/--sync, DriveItem/DiskItem, --dry_run) onto dodomorandi's modern deps. In the meantime, document the existing download skip behavior.
issues.notes: Most-requested item in this batch (8 reactions), and it also covers #69/#65. Drive allows duplicate names (prasmussen's concern in #16), so fail on ambiguous matches as toutizes does. Skipping unchanged files is the biggest real-world speedup for repeat backups.

issues.title: Select a different drive

issues.title: Implement .gdriveignore
issues.still_relevant_reason: Recursive upload walks every entry with fs::read_dir and no filtering (file_tree.rs:114-130). No ignore/exclude option exists anywhere in src/, nor in either fork.
issues.recommendation: Add repeatable '--exclude <glob>' plus an optional .gdriveignore (gitignore syntax) using the 'ignore' crate's WalkBuilder in FileTree::from_path, and apply the same globs as a name filter for recursive download.
issues.notes: Fits naturally with #84 sync for backup workflows.

issues.title: << Restarting upload >>
issues.still_relevant_reason: Upload sessions only survive inside one process: UploadDelegate keeps the resumable URL in memory (delegate.rs:30,82-88). Retries within a run work (100000 attempts, upload.rs:43), but if the process dies the session URI is lost and the next run starts from byte 0.
issues.recommendation: Save the resumable session URI to a state file (e.g. config_dir/uploads/<hash of path+size+mtime+parent>.json) in store_upload_url and return it from upload_url() on the next run. The generated client then queries the server for the committed range and resumes (google-drive3 api.rs:9078 upload_url path; google-apis-common query_transfer_status lib.rs:606-665). Expire entries after about 7 days, and pair with #84 skip-existing for directory restarts.
issues.notes: Low demand but cheap given the existing delegate hooks, and valuable for multi-GB uploads.

issues.title: /root/.gdrive/ folde  Permissions for PHP exec

That only works without registration for 'Desktop app' clients, so 'Web application' clients get redirect_uri_mismatch. The doc says Desktop app (docs/create_google_api_credentials.md step 22) but is written for the pre-2025 Cloud Console. Step 24 ('you may find them again later') is wrong now that new client secrets are shown only once.
issues.recommendation: Rewrite create_google_api_credentials.md for the current Google Auth Platform UI (Branding/Audience/Clients/Data access), stress 'Desktop app', and add a troubleshooting table (redirect_uri_mismatch -> wrong client type; 127.0.0.1 refused -> remote server, see #114; 7-day expiry -> Testing mode). Validate client_id format in `account add` and print the expected client type.
issues.notes: Carries the 'Google OAuth onboarding' theme in this batch (#109, #115, #120, #121, plus #22, #30, #35, #60, #129, #160 elsewhere). Thread comments mix in the remote-server case (#114/#125).

issues.title: No Drive Listed when running `gdrive drives list`

issues.title: Add to README: how to download files from public Google Drive
issues.still_relevant_reason: Every command needs an OAuth account (hub_helper::get_hub, src/common/hub_helper.rs:11-21). There is no anonymous or API-key mode, and commands take IDs, not URLs (the user passed a folder URL to `files copy`).

issues.title: could not load platform certs
issues.still_relevant_reason: src/hub.rs:33-34 uses HttpsConnectorBuilder::with_native_roots(). In the pinned hyper-rustls 0.23.2 (config.rs:31) this calls .expect("could not load platform certs"), so gdrive panics on hosts without a CA bundle (minimal containers, CI images) or with a corrupt macOS trust store. dodomorandi (hyper-rustls 0.27, src/hub.rs:24) turns the panic into an io::Error but still fails.
issues.recommendation: After the dependency upgrade, build the TLS config with native roots and fall back to bundled webpki-roots (hyper-rustls feature `webpki-roots`), or use rustls-platform-verifier, and warn instead of failing. Document SSL_CERT_FILE / installing ca-certificates.
issues.notes: The static musl binary is popular in Docker/CI, where missing /etc/ssl/certs is common. The second comment matches #58 (macOS 'Trust Settings Record was corrupted').

issues.title: How to send data back to Script (from local Browser)
issues.still_relevant_reason: Headless auth is still impossible without tunnels or export/import. The flow only prints a URL and waits on 127.0.0.1:8085 (src/hub.rs:64-67,105-111). The leftover OOB redirect_uris in hub.rs:83 is unused (Google blocked OOB in 2023). Neither fork adds a manual mode.
issues.recommendation: Add `account add --manual` (alias --no-browser): print the auth URL, have the user paste the full redirected http://127.0.0.1:8085/?code=... URL, extract the code and exchange it. yup-oauth2 supports this via InstalledFlowReturnMethod::Interactive plus a delegate that overrides redirect_uri() to the loopback URI (yup-oauth2 12.1.2 installed.rs:145-170, authenticator_delegate.rs:108). Also merge PR #132's SSH-tunnel doc and the curl trick from #161.
issues.notes: Google's device-code flow cannot be used, because it does not allow the full `drive` scope. The iptables DNAT workaround in the thread is insecure, which makes a built-in manual mode more valuable. Remote-server setup is a recurring complaint (#33, #109, #125 with 5 reactions, #139, #161).

issues.title: Access blocked: Authorization Error
issues.still_relevant_reason: 'Doesn't comply with Google's OAuth 2.0 policy' + Error 400 invalid_request is what Google returns for the blocked OOB flow (gdrive2), and for loopback redirects on a non-Desktop client type. gdrive v3 uses the allowed loopback flow (src/hub.rs:66). The reporter says it 'worked before', which suggests gdrive2 or a Web-type client. The 2025 comment has no details.
issues.recommendation: Document it in the auth troubleshooting section (#109): use gdrive v3, create a 'Desktop app' client, add yourself as a test user or publish the app. When the token exchange fails, print the client type hint and a link to the troubleshooting doc.

issues.title: [Request] Isn't there a sync option?
issues.still_relevant_reason: Upstream has no sync. Upload --recursive always creates a new folder tree (src/main.rs:196 help text) and download aborts or overwrites with no skip-unchanged logic. toutizes implements upload/download --sync: md5 compare to skip identical files, delete extraneous files, --dry-run, and parallel workers (toutizes src/main.rs:185-292, src/files/upload.rs:219-296, src/common/disk_item.rs:122-245).
issues.recommendation: Port toutizes' sync semantics (skip identical by md5, --overwrite vs --sync with deletes, --dry-run, parallel TaskManager) onto the modernized dodomorandi base, as `files sync` or `upload|download --sync`. This is the main 'faster transfers' win: unchanged files are never re-sent.
issues.notes: High aggregate demand across #16, #84 (8 reactions), #116 and #56/#152 (--skip). toutizes is on the old deps, so expect a port, not a cherry-pick.

issues.title: Cannot filter by name
issues.still_relevant_reason: src/main.rs:476-480 does `parent_query.or(drive_query).unwrap_or(query)`, so --query is silently dropped whenever --parent or --drive is given. Both forks keep the same code (dodomorandi main.rs:510-512, toutizes main.rs:585-590).

For --drive, use corpora=drive + driveId (list.rs:98-104) instead of an `in parents` query, so the whole shared drive is searchable. Error if --query already contains 'in parents' and --parent is also given.

issues.title: Bad request: File not found when using in Gitlab CI

issues.title: Add auth code manually
issues.still_relevant_reason: Upstream supports only the loopback flow: oauth2::InstalledFlowReturnMethod::HTTPPortRedirect(8085) at src/hub.rs:64-71. The delegate (src/hub.rs:95-111) only prints the URL and ignores need_code. There is no way to paste a code or redirect URL. The README workaround (README.md:44-51) is to add the account locally, then export and import it. Google blocked the OOB/manual-code flow (urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob, still listed at hub.rs:83 but unused) in Jan 2023, so yup-oauth2's Interactive mode is not an option.
issues.recommendation: Add a headless 'paste the redirect URL' mode to `account add` (for example `--no-browser`). Keep the loopback listener, and also read stdin: when the user pastes the http://127.0.0.1:8085/?code=... URL their local browser failed to load, gdrive sends that GET to its own listener, automating the #161 curl trick. Also make the port configurable and merge PR #132's SSH-tunnel docs.
issues.notes: This is the top headless pain point; related issues are #33, #139 and #161, and #161 confirms the redirect-replay approach works. Google's device-code flow is not a fallback, because it does not allow the full `drive` scope. Neither fork changes the auth flow (both still use HTTPPortRedirect(8085)).

issues.title: Missing DLLs on windows

Neither fork changes this.
issues.recommendation: Build Windows releases with a static CRT: `[target.x86_64-pc-windows-msvc] rustflags=["-C","target-feature=+crt-static"]` in .cargo/config.toml, or RUSTFLAGS in CI. Add an aarch64-pc-windows-msvc artifact, and document the VC++ redistributable as a fallback.
issues.notes: The 2026 comment reports error 0xC000000B on a fresh machine, another runtime/loader failure. The reporter's own fix was installing the VC++ redistributable. Related to #122.

issues.title: Non-interactive mode
issues.still_relevant_reason: Every command builds an InstalledFlowAuthenticator with the interactive delegate (src/common/hub_helper.rs:11-21 calls src/hub.rs:56-75). When refresh fails, yup-oauth2 falls back to the full browser flow: the delegate prints a URL and returns Ok (hub.rs:105-111), then the process waits forever on 127.0.0.1:8085 with no timeout. The next cron run then fails with 'Address in use' (#149, #33). There is no --non-interactive flag, TTY check or timeout in upstream or either fork.

Add a timeout to the loopback wait. Longer term, support service accounts (#49) for unattended jobs.

issues.title: Question: Has gdrive3 aligned or surpassed gdrive2 these days?

issues.title: Error: Failed to get access token: error creating server listener: Address in use (os error 98)
issues.still_relevant_reason: The port is hard-coded (InstalledFlowReturnMethod::HTTPPortRedirect(8085), src/hub.rs:66) and the auth wait has no timeout, so a previous gdrive process stuck waiting for OAuth holds 8085 and every new auth attempt fails. The reporter's `ss` output showed gdrive itself listening, and `pkill gdrive` fixed it.

issues.title: 【Windows】refresh_token is null in tokens.json
issues.still_relevant_reason: Google returns a refresh_token only on a user's first consent for a client unless prompt=consent is sent. yup-oauth2 8.1.0 builds the auth URL with access_type=offline but no prompt (yup-oauth2-8.1.0/src/installed.rs:55-60), and gdrive neither adds it nor checks the result (src/account/add.rs:20-47). Re-adding an account already authorized on another machine or OS therefore stores refresh_token null, and the account dies after about 1 hour.
issues.recommendation: Force consent. On yup-oauth2 12 (dodomorandi stack), call .force_account_selection(true) on the InstalledFlowAuthenticator builder (yup-oauth2-12.1.2/src/authenticator.rs:698, which adds prompt=select_account+consent). On the old stack, append &prompt=consent to the URL printed in hub.rs:105-111. After `account add`, fail or warn if tokens.json lacks a refresh_token.
issues.notes: The Windows-only angle is probably coincidence: the reporter likely authorized the same client elsewhere first. This is my diagnosis, not reproduced. Neither fork sets force_account_selection.

issues.title: Terminal Not Responding After Authorization
issues.still_relevant_reason: The browser reached the loopback server ('You may now close this window'), so the hang comes afterwards: the token exchange to oauth2.googleapis.com and the about.get call. gdrive's hyper client ignores HTTP(S)_PROXY and system proxy settings (src/hub.rs:31-43, no proxy support), and no timeouts are set. Behind a firewall that requires a proxy, where only the browser has a proxy configured, the request hangs and then errors.
issues.recommendation: Add proxy support honoring HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY/NO_PROXY plus a `--proxy` flag. On the new stack use hyper-util's proxy matcher or move to reqwest; do not port PR #141's unmaintained hyper-proxy 0.9. Add connect and request timeouts with clear errors.

issues.title: --skip functionality exists but is not well documented
issues.still_relevant_reason: The --overwrite help says 'Overwrite existing files and folders' (src/main.rs:162-164), but recursive download skips any local file whose MD5 matches (src/files/download.rs:162-168, local_file_is_identical at 406-421) and only re-downloads files that differ. Without --overwrite, the run aborts on an existing root (download.rs:82, 333-356). This resume-friendly behavior is undocumented, and there is no --skip (#56).
issues.recommendation: Rewrite the --overwrite help and docs to say identical files are skipped by MD5. Add an explicit `--skip-existing` (skip by name or size without hashing, which is faster on huge trees). Make recursive download continue on per-file errors (#136) so long transfers resume cheaply.
issues.notes: Resuming large transfers is speed-related. toutizes documents that identical files are not downloaded with --overwrite, adds --sync, and lets per-task failures not abort the run (src/files/download.rs:255-262).

ListQuery::FilesOnDrive (src/files/list.rs:161-163) only lists `'<drive>' in parents`, and list_files never sets corpora=drive or driveId (list.rs:98-108), so a query cannot search a whole shared drive. Both forks have the same line (dodomorandi main.rs:510-512, toutizes main.rs:585-590).
issues.recommendation: Make --query an Option. Combine filters as `(<query>) and '<parent>' in parents`. For --drive, call .corpora("drive").drive_id(id) with include_items_from_all_drives, and use the query (default `trashed = false`) instead of the top-level-only parents filter. Add a unit test for query composition.
issues.notes: Because clap's default_value_t for query (main.rs:129) is RootNotTrashed, the code currently cannot tell whether the user passed --query.

pulls.title: Concurrent directory download
pulls.author: Defman
pulls.summary: Draft PR. Replaces recursive download with a lazy streaming traversal: stream::unfold over a DFS stack of folders (one files.list per folder) yields each folder's non-folder files, .flatten() feeds them into .buffer_unordered(N), with N from a new `--concurent` flag. save_body_to_file is rewritten to async tokio::fs, with md5 computed through tokio_util InspectReader and create_dir_all per file. Adds an ext.rs FileExtension trait, derives Default on ListFilesConfig, and adds the tokio-stream and tokio-util deps. It also comments out single-file download and shortcut following.
pulls.quality_notes: The concurrency design is sound: in-flight downloads are capped at N, the folder walk is lazy and memory-bounded, and listing overlaps with downloads. Folder listing is serial, so deep trees of tiny folders become listing-bound. The PR is an unfinished draft that breaks existing behaviour: `gdrive files download <file-id>` does nothing (the download_regular call is commented out); --follow-shortcuts does nothing; `--concurent` is a required usize with no default, so every download call must pass it; `--concurent 0` hangs forever (futures-util 0.3.25 BufferUnordered with max=0 returns Pending without a waker). All results are collected into a Vec and dropped, and the function always returns Ok, so download, write and listing errors are swallowed; listing errors are even remapped to MissingFileName ('TODO: fix error'). MD5 verification is removed (expected_md5=None) and so is the skip-identical-local-file check. Google Docs are no longer filtered (the old FileTreeDrive kept only is_binary files), so they fail silently on alt=media. Introduced race: tmp path file_path.with_extension("incomplete") replaces the extension, so 'a.pdf' and 'a.docx' (or Drive's allowed duplicate names) in one folder write the same 'a.incomplete' concurrently, giving a corrupt file plus a failed rename, all silent.

pulls.title: 🏎️ Speed up uploading by parallelizing uploads
pulls.author: Jasper-Bekkers
pulls.summary: In `files upload --recursive`, replaces the per-folder sequential file loop with futures::future::join_all over all files of that folder, so each folder's files upload concurrently. Folders are still created one by one, parent first. The rest of the diff is rustfmt of #41's code (file_helper.rs, common/mod.rs, update.rs, upload.rs). The author calls it 'one-off throw-away code' and reports reaching 1 Gbps.
pulls.quality_notes: Proof of concept. Fan-out is unbounded: one in-flight upload per file in the folder. join_all collects the iterator eagerly, so every file is fs::File::open'ed before any upload starts, and the open error is .unwrap()'ed. A folder with more files than `ulimit -n` (1024 on Linux, 256 on macOS) panics mid-upload and leaves a partial tree on Drive. Memory: google-drive3/google-apis-common read the whole body (simple upload, files up to the chunk size) or one full chunk (resumable, default 32 MiB) into a Vec per in-flight upload, using blocking read_to_end. That costs N x up to 32 MiB of RAM (1000 x 20 MB photos is about 20 GB), and each blocking disk read stalls every other upload sharing the single join_all task. The Vec<Result> returned by join_all is dropped, so failed uploads are ignored silently, the success summary still prints and the exit code is 0. --print-only-id lines are printed before the upload instead of after success. The per-folder barrier means trees of many small folders gain little.
superseded_by: toutizes fork: parallel upload via TaskManager + tokio Semaphore (src/files/tasks.rs, src/files/upload.rs, global --workers)
pulls.recommendation_reason: Right idea: IdGen pre-generates the IDs, so the file uploads are independent once their folder exists. Wrong implementation. On the dodomorandi base: create all folders first, parent-first (optionally in parallel per depth level, since the IDs are known), then push all files through one global bounded pool (`--parallel N`, default about 4, stream::buffer_unordered or JoinSet plus a Semaphore with tokio::spawn and Arc<Hub>). Open files lazily inside the task, aggregate per-file results into a summary and a non-zero exit, budget memory as N x chunk_size, and fix the delegate retry policy (see notes).
pulls.notes: Interaction with src/common/delegate.rs and src/files/upload.rs: every upload_file() builds its own UploadDelegate, so each file has an independent Backoff (min 1 s, max 60 s, max_retries 100000) and its own in-memory resumable session URL. Nothing is shared or global: when Drive throttles, all N uploads back off and retry independently (thundering herd), and one file stuck on persistent 5xx keeps join_all, and the whole command, waiting almost indefinitely. should_retry() retries only 5xx and 429. Drive reports most rate limiting as 403 rateLimitExceeded/userRateLimitExceeded, and also 408 (issue #36); those abort at once, and under #82 they turn into silent data loss. The JSON error body passed to http_failure is ignored, though it carries the reason. Backoff.attempts is never reset after a successful chunk, so late retries in long uploads sleep close to 60 s. Ordering is safe: folder IDs are pre-generated and folders are created before their files. HTTP: hub.rs enables h1+h2 and googleapis negotiates h2, so the parallel uploads share one TCP connection. The gains come from overlapping per-request latency (large for many small files, smaller for a few big files), and an h1 connection pool is worth benchmarking. Drive quotas (per-minute query quotas, the 750 GB/day per-user upload cap, undocumented sustained create rate) are neither respected nor surfaced. git apply: clean on upstream main. Conflicts on dodomorandi (upload.rs/update.rs/file_helper.rs refactored; UploadDelegate borrows &UploadDelegateConfig). Also conflicts with #67, which carries the same rustfmt hunks. dodomorandi uploads sequentially; google-drive3 7 / google-apis-common 8 there still buffer a chunk with blocking read_to_end, so the memory analysis also holds on that base.
