pulls.notes: Compared with #144 (another agent's batch): the pagination loop is nearly identical. #144 mirrors files::list (usize, remaining-aware page_size, default 10) but drags in .idea/ files, a Cargo.lock v4 bump and unrelated edits to upload.rs, update.rs and hub.rs. #156 is the cleaner diff and #144 has the better types; combine them. Neither dodo nor toutizes paginates drives.list.

pulls.title: Add TUI navigate mode
pulls.author: stulluk
pulls.summary: Adds a `gdrive navigate` ratatui/crossterm TUI (src/navigate.rs, 1503 lines): browse folders, download a single file with progress, upload a file or folder with progress through a picker, delete with y/n confirmation, and confirm before quitting during transfers. The PR also includes #158's Docker ARM scripts, a .cursorignore file, a README section and a Cargo.lock rewritten to lockfile v4 (ratatui 0.26.3, crossterm 0.27, proc-macro2/quote bumps).
pulls.quality_notes: The code is readable but has design and correctness problems. The whole UI runs in spawn_blocking and calls Handle::block_on for listing and deleting, so it freezes during network calls; transfers run on ad-hoc std::threads that also block_on. Any error from reload() (refresh, opening a folder, going back) propagates out and quits the TUI. files::delete prints 'Deleted ...' to stdout inside the alternate screen and corrupts it. Delete is permanent (not trash) and recursive for folders. Listing is silently capped at 1000 items. Folder download is refused, although the PR body says directories work, and Google Docs and shortcuts are unsupported. It duplicates download.rs's save/MD5 logic. There is no panic hook to restore the terminal, and retries are hard-coded to max_retries 100000. It bundles unrelated files.
pulls.recommendation_reason: Out of scope for a scriptable CLI. It adds about 1.8k lines plus TUI dependencies, has no tests, and would block the dependency migration and refactors. If anyone ever wants a TUI, it belongs in a separate binary or crate (or behind a non-default cargo feature) built on a stable library API. Only the ProgressReader idea is worth keeping.
pulls.notes: Worth keeping: ProgressReader<R: Read+Seek>, which wraps the upload source to report bytes read, and the streaming progress counter in the download loop. That is a cheap way to add indicatif progress bars to the plain CLI (issues #12 and #44, the most-requested UX items). The lockfile churn conflicts with dodo's dependency migration.

pulls.title: Add Docker scripts for ARM static builds
pulls.author: stulluk
pulls.summary: Adds a trivial Dockerfile (FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}, WORKDIR /work), dockerbuild.sh (picks messense/rust-musl-cross:aarch64-musl or :armv7-musleabihf and builds a local image) and indockerbuild.sh (runs cargo build --release --target <t> in that image and copies the binary to dist/<t>/), plus README instructions. Local builds only, no CI.
pulls.quality_notes: It does what it says, and it is the only PR in this batch that covers armv7 (32-bit Raspberry Pi). The Dockerfile/image step adds nothing: you can `docker run` the messense image directly. The container runs as root, so target/ and dist/ end up root-owned on Linux hosts. There is no cargo registry cache volume, so every run downloads all crates again. Scripts sit in the repo root. Not exercised here: I did not build the images.
pulls.recommendation_reason: Ship armv7-unknown-linux-musleabihf (and maybe arm-unknown-linux-musleabi for Pi Zero/1) from CI using cargo-zigbuild or cross. Document `cross build --target ...` (or a single docker run line with --user and a registry cache) for local builds rather than committing three script files.
pulls.notes: The same files are also included in #157. #130 (another agent) does armv7 and aarch64 in CI by cross-compiling with clang and rust-lld. dodo uses rustls 0.23 with ring 0.17 and no aws-lc-rs, so zig/cross cross-compiles need only a C cross compiler.

pulls.title: Add support for Markdown file type and MIME type
pulls.author: lev-n
pulls.summary: Adds Md / text/markdown (export of Docs to .md, md in the import map) and fixes import mime handling: FileInfo gets source_mime_type, import.rs fills it from the file extension, and upload_file sends it as the media Content-Type while the metadata mimeType stays the Google Docs target type.
pulls.quality_notes: Complete and correct. Separating source and target mime is what the Drive API expects for conversions, and it also makes csv, docx, jpg and other imports send accurate media types instead of relying on content sniffing. Small diff, compiles cleanly, tested manually by the author for export and import. Nits: adding an Option field to FileInfo is a bit ad hoc (an explicit upload_mime parameter would be cleaner); the `files import` help text was not updated (#146 did that); ext.get_export_mime() is reused for an import-side lookup, so the name reads oddly.
pulls.recommendation_reason: It is the better of the two Markdown PRs and would be merge-as-is on upstream. On the dodo base it needs a mechanical port (pub(crate) consts, LazyLock mime statics, a reshaped file_info::Config). Add #146's help-text line when porting.
pulls.notes: It conflicts with dodo in drive_file.rs, file_info.rs, file_tree.rs, import.rs and upload.rs, but 3-way conflicts are only context changes. dodo's import.rs and upload_file have the same single-mime logic as upstream, so the fix still applies conceptually. Neither fork has Markdown.

pulls.title: Recursive download: add export
pulls.author: serebrov
pulls.summary: `files download --recursive` now exports Google Docs, Sheets and Slides to docx, xlsx and pptx (new DocType::default_office_export_type) instead of silently skipping them. It also replaces 'build the whole FileTreeDrive, then download' with a streaming recursive walk (list a folder, download or export its files, recurse) that prints a summary at the end.
pulls.quality_notes: Works and compiles. Problems: (1) the file_tree_drive.rs changes (from_google_doc, is_google_doc, the mime_type field) are dead code, because the second commit stops using FileTreeDrive at all; the whole module is now unused, and no warning appears only because pub items in bin crates are not linted by default; (2) one failed export (for example Drive's 10 MB export limit) aborts the entire recursive download with `?`; (3) export is always on, with no flag to choose a format or opt out; (4) exports are redone on every run with no change detection; (5) a missing folder id reports Error::MissingFileName; (6) Drawings, Forms and shortcuts are still silently skipped; (7) '/' in names (#19) and long names (#53) are not handled; (8) the md5-mismatch warning was lost.
pulls.recommendation_reason: The feature is wanted: whole-drive backup with Docs (issues #64 and #123, and the documented 'Docs silently ignored' limitation). Port the improved version from #164 (same author: exports warn instead of abort, shortcuts, filename sanitizing, mtime) onto dodo's download module. Add a --export-format or --skip-docs option and delete the dead FileTreeDrive code.
pulls.notes: Speed: the streaming walk starts the first download sooner and prints progress, but the total API calls and transfer time are unchanged (still sequential). Parallel recursive download is in PR #68 and toutizes' TaskManager. Upstream already has default_export_type (pdf/csv/pdf); office formats are better for backups because CSV keeps only the first sheet (#98). Pre-existing bug, also present in dodo: the temp file is file_path.with_extension("incomplete"), so a.pdf and a.txt share a.incomplete.

pulls.title: Add short flag for common CLI arguments
pulls.author: antoine2711
pulls.summary: Adds clap short aliases: -m/--max, -q/--query, -p/--parent (list, upload, mkdir, import), -r/--recursive (download, upload, delete), -s/--chunk-size (upload, update).
pulls.quality_notes: Tiny and correct. I built a debug binary, where clap's debug assertions are active, ran --help on all seven touched subcommands, and found no short-flag collisions. -p matches gdrive v2 habits (issues #1 and #5). The PR body omits that delete also gets -r.
pulls.recommendation_reason: Re-apply on dodo's restructured main.rs, where the patch conflicts. Settle the short-flag namespace first: toutizes already uses -r recursive, -f overwrite and -s sync on download/upload, so if sync or overwrite semantics are adopted, -s should not mean --chunk-size. A one-key -r on delete may also deserve a second thought.
pulls.notes: dodo has no short flags. toutizes has -r, -f and -s (see its main.rs lines 205-291).

pulls.title: Fix dependency update problem
pulls.author: serebrov
pulls.summary: Accidental PR of serebrov's fork main; the author says it was meant for his own repo. It is NOT a migration to google-drive3 7.x. It contains: (a) a Cargo.lock regenerated with `cargo update` inside the OLD semver ranges (lockfile v4; hyper 0.14.23 to 0.14.32, tokio 1.24 to 1.54, clap 4.0 to 4.6, 51 crates added, 30 removed, 133 bumped), keeping google-drive3 5.0.2-beta from the prasmussen git fork, hyper-rustls 0.23.2 and rustls 0.20, plus a direct `yup-oauth2 = "=8.1.0"` pin, so that `cargo update` no longer pulls in a second hyper-rustls (0.24) and breaks the build with the enable_http2 error from issue #131; (b) everything in #162, plus Google Drawings export (png/svg/pdf), shortcut handling (symlink when the target is in the tree, otherwise download or export it), '/' to '_' and 255-byte filename sanitizing, mtime preservation via the new filetime dependency, mtime-based skipping of unchanged exports, warnings instead of aborts for failed exports, a warning for unsupported google-apps types, and modifiedTime/shortcutDetails added to the files.list fields; (c) README replaced with the fork's own README.
pulls.quality_notes: The most complete recursive backup implementation among the PRs, and it compiles. Bugs: sanitize_filename computes MAX_FILENAME_BYTES - ext.len(), which underflows and panics when the 'extension' after the last '.' exceeds 255 bytes; exported names are sanitized and then get '.docx' appended, so they can reach 260 bytes and fail with ENAMETOOLONG; only '/' is replaced, not the characters Windows forbids. Shortcuts: downloaded_files maps only files, so a shortcut to a folder inside the tree downloads that folder a second time; shortcuts found while processing shortcuts are pushed after std::mem::take and silently dropped; shortcut targets are downloaded with no md5 check or skip, so they are re-downloaded every run; non-unix platforms only get a warning. Same-name collisions are not handled. The yup-oauth2 pin is a workaround, not a fix. The README is hijacked, with personal paths and OAuth client names.
superseded_by: dodomorandi fork (real dependency migration: google-drive3 7.0, google-apis-common 8, hyper 1, hyper-rustls 0.27, yup-oauth2 12)
pulls.recommendation_reason: Drop the Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock part (dodo's migration makes the pin unnecessary) and the README. Port the download.rs logic (export with warnings, Drawings, shortcuts, sanitize_filename with the underflow and Windows fixes, filetime mtime, skip-unchanged) onto dodo's download module. It supersedes #162.
pulls.notes: Speed: it skips re-exporting unchanged Docs (mtime match), which speeds up repeated backups, but it still MD5-hashes every existing local binary file on every run. Now that mtime is preserved, a size+mtime fast path before MD5 would make incremental runs much faster. It does nothing for parallelism. The pin explains issue #131: building on a host without the pinned lock, or after `cargo update`, mixes hyper-rustls 0.23 and 0.24.
